9 · Shared state and branch isolation

All six branches ran against ONE DesignState, which is the production shape. A rejected patch is only harmless if it can be shown to be inert, so the state hash and the full entity inventory were taken before each call and compared after.

Two different isolation claims live on this page, and only one of them is hard. An s03a view carries no topology at all - the pass does not read what it writes - so "no foreign topology" there is largely structural. The real test is section 10: those views DO carry topology, and each branch saw only its own while 132 topology entities from the other five stood in the same DesignState. The namespace-occupancy block carried every spent id into each later prompt, and no candidate collided with an earlier one.

10 · S03b readiness — actual consumer views, zero calls

Built with the real s03b responsibility against the final shared state, one invocation branch at a time. The S03b model was not called.

What s03b authors - PhysicalInteraction, ConstraintRelation, LoadPath, AssemblyStep and the derived mobility grid - is absent from these views by construction, and its absence is not counted here as a gap: a branch that already carried them would mean s03b had run. load_case and physical_obligation are design-wide and are the same for every branch by declaration; what differs per branch is the topology it is being asked to reason about.

Counted by SEMANTIC ROLE, read from the s03b responsibility's required premise classes through the view's own required minimum. An earlier version of this page counted from a family list written into the report generator, and that list held neither Joint nor Interface - so it printed zero topology relations for every branch while the contract declares topology_relation: [Interface, Joint]. It also called the retention premise class "retention-worded obligations" and counted them by matching the word in the text; the contract satisfies that class with the physical_obligation role, which is every Obligation.

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.\n\n  bodies[]             id \"BOD-0001\", role, instance_identity,\n                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body\n                       is the reason for; [] if none)\n  rigid_groups[]       id \"RGP-0001\", body, members[], is_default (boolean)\n  joints[]             id \"JNT-0001\", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,\n                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]\n                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed\n                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. [\"FRM-JNT-0001\"].\n                       \"+Z\" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that\n                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the\n                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later\n                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.\n                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint\n                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,\n                       and [] is the right answer there.\n                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT\n                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another\n                       object:\n                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,\n                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,\n                         activation_window\n                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real\n                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this\n                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so\n                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence\n                       that the mechanism deflects itself.\n                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.\n                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have\n                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not\n                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as\n                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result\n                       nothing here computed.\n  interfaces[]         id \"IFC-0001\", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,\n                       addresses_obligations[]\n  configurations[]     id \"CFG-0001\", name, kind, bodies_present[],\n                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}\n                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the\n                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the\n                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required\n                       to differ. rendered prompt (40475 chars)

You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW
   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.
   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are
   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left
   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the
   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable
   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-
   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a
   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups
   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at
   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.
6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it
   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could
   cross.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity,
                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body
                       is the reason for; [] if none)
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]
                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed
                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. ["FRM-JNT-0001"].
                       "+Z" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that
                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the
                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later
                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.
                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint
                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,
                       and [] is the right answer there.
                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT
                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another
                       object:
                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,
                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,
                         activation_window
                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real
                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this
                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so
                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence
                       that the mechanism deflects itself.
                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.
                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have
                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not
                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as
                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result
                       nothing here computed.
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,
                       addresses_obligations[]
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[],
                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}
                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the
                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the
                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required
                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and
                       is checked against it, so a name is never what
                       distinguishes two states
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[],
                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for
                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),
                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region
                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the
                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from
                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the
                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor
                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on
                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)
  unresolved[]         id "S3U-0001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT
  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ
  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE
  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

IDS YOU EMIT ARE NEW
Every id in your response is one you are creating now. The typed input already
contains ids of its own, and reusing one of them does not extend that entity, it
collides with it. Use exactly the prefixes shown above and never an id that
already appears in the input.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
  rigid_groups[].body            a body id you emit
  joints[].parent_group/child_group  rigid group ids you emit
  interfaces[].bodies            body ids you emit
  configurations[].bodies_present body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].reach_targets functional region ids you emit
  functional_regions[].required_by_actors actor ids from the input
  joints[].frame_ids             frame names you coin here
  bodies[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  interfaces[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].rigid_group  a rigid group id you emit
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].differs_from configuration ids you emit
  unresolved[].kept_open_by      Ambiguity or Freedom ids from the input, and
                                 nothing else - not a requirement, not a body
  unresolved[].alternatives      when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS these are
                                 entity ids; otherwise they are not ids at all

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. You are naming the\n                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later\n                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.\n                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint\n                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,\n                       and [] is the right answer there.\n                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT\n                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another\n                       object:\n                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,\n                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,\n                         activation_window\n                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real\n                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this\n                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so\n                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence\n                       that the mechanism deflects itself.\n                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.\n                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have\n                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not\n                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as\n                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result\n                       nothing here computed.\n  interfaces[]         id \"IFC-0001\", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,\n                       addresses_obligations[]\n  configurations[]     id \"CFG-0001\", name, kind, bodies_present[],\n                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}\n                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the\n                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the\n                       named sibling configurations. rendered prompt (40856 chars)

You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW
   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.
   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are
   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left
   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the
   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable
   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-
   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a
   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups
   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at
   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.
6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it
   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could
   cross.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity,
                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body
                       is the reason for; [] if none)
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]
                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed
                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. ["FRM-JNT-0001"].
                       "+Z" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that
                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the
                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later
                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.
                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint
                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,
                       and [] is the right answer there.
                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT
                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another
                       object:
                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,
                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,
                         activation_window
                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real
                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this
                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so
                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence
                       that the mechanism deflects itself.
                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.
                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have
                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not
                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as
                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result
                       nothing here computed.
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,
                       addresses_obligations[]
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[],
                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}
                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the
                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the
                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required
                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and
                       is checked against it, so a name is never what
                       distinguishes two states
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[],
                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for
                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),
                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region
                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the
                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from
                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the
                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor
                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on
                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)
  unresolved[]         id "S3U-0001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT
  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ
  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE
  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

IDS YOU EMIT ARE NEW
Every id in your response is one you are creating now. The typed input already
contains ids of its own, and reusing one of them does not extend that entity, it
collides with it. Use exactly the prefixes shown above and never an id that
already appears in the input.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
  rigid_groups[].body            a body id you emit
  joints[].parent_group/child_group  rigid group ids you emit
  interfaces[].bodies            body ids you emit
  configurations[].bodies_present body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].reach_targets functional region ids you emit
  functional_regions[].required_by_actors actor ids from the input
  joints[].frame_ids             frame names you coin here
  bodies[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  interfaces[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].rigid_group  a rigid group id you emit
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].differs_from configuration ids you emit
  unresolved[].kept_open_by      Ambiguity or Freedom ids from the input, and
                                 nothing else - not a requirement, not a body
  unresolved[].alternatives      when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS these are
                                 entity ids; otherwise they are not ids at all

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.\n\n  bodies[]             id \"BOD-0001\", role, instance_identity,\n                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body\n                       is the reason for; [] if none)\n  rigid_groups[]       id \"RGP-0001\", body, members[], is_default (boolean)\n  joints[]             id \"JNT-0001\", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,\n                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]\n                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed\n                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. [\"FRM-JNT-0001\"].\n                       \"+Z\" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that\n                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the\n                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later\n                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.\n                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint\n                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,\n                       and [] is the right answer there.\n                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT\n                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another\n                       object:\n                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,\n                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,\n                         activation_window\n                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real\n                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this\n                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so\n                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence\n                       that the mechanism deflects itself.\n                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.\n                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have\n                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not\n                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as\n                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result\n                       nothing here computed.\n  interfaces[]         id \"IFC-0001\", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,\n                       addresses_obligations[]\n  configurations[]     id \"CFG-0001\", name, kind, bodies_present[],\n                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}\n                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the\n                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the\n                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required\n                       to differ. rendered prompt (41160 chars)

You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW
   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.
   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are
   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left
   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the
   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable
   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-
   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a
   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups
   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at
   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.
6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it
   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could
   cross.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity,
                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body
                       is the reason for; [] if none)
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]
                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed
                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. ["FRM-JNT-0001"].
                       "+Z" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that
                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the
                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later
                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.
                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint
                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,
                       and [] is the right answer there.
                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT
                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another
                       object:
                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,
                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,
                         activation_window
                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real
                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this
                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so
                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence
                       that the mechanism deflects itself.
                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.
                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have
                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not
                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as
                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result
                       nothing here computed.
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,
                       addresses_obligations[]
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[],
                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}
                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the
                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the
                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required
                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and
                       is checked against it, so a name is never what
                       distinguishes two states
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[],
                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for
                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),
                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region
                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the
                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from
                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the
                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor
                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on
                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)
  unresolved[]         id "S3U-0001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT

  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.\n\n  bodies[]             id \"BOD-0001\", role, instance_identity,\n                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body\n                       is the reason for; [] if none)\n  rigid_groups[]       id \"RGP-0001\", body, members[], is_default (boolean)\n  joints[]             id \"JNT-0001\", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,\n                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]\n                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed\n                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. [\"FRM-JNT-0001\"].\n                       \"+Z\" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that\n                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the\n                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later\n                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.\n                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint\n                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,\n                       and [] is the right answer there.\n                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT\n                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another\n                       object:\n                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,\n                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,\n                         activation_window\n                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real\n                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this\n                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so\n                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence\n                       that the mechanism deflects itself.\n                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.\n                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have\n                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not\n                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as\n                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result\n                       nothing here computed.\n  interfaces[]         id \"IFC-0001\", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,\n                       addresses_obligations[]\n  configurations[]     id \"CFG-0001\", name, kind, bodies_present[],\n                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}\n                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the\n                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the\n                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required\n                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and\n                       is checked against it, so a name is never what\n                       distinguishes two states\n  functional_regions[] id \"FRG-0001\", role, owning_bodies[],\n                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for\n                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),\n                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region\n                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the\n                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from\n                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the\n                       destination. rendered prompt (41460 chars)

You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW
   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.
   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are
   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left
   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the
   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable
   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-
   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a
   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups
   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at
   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.
6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it
   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could
   cross.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity,
                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body
                       is the reason for; [] if none)
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]
                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed
                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. ["FRM-JNT-0001"].
                       "+Z" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that
                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the
                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later
                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.
                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint
                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,
                       and [] is the right answer there.
                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT
                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another
                       object:
                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,
                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,
                         activation_window
                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real
                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this
                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so
                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence
                       that the mechanism deflects itself.
                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.
                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have
                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not
                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as
                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result
                       nothing here computed.
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,
                       addresses_obligations[]
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[],
                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}
                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the
                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the
                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required
                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and
                       is checked against it, so a name is never what
                       distinguishes two states
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[],
                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for
                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),
                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region
                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the
                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from
                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the
                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor
                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on
                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)
  unresolved[]         id "S3U-0001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT
  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ
  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE
  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

IDS YOU EMIT ARE NEW
Every id in your response is one you are creating now. The typed input already
contains ids of its own, and reusing one of them does not extend that entity, it
collides with it. Use exactly the prefixes shown above and never an id that
already appears in the input.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
  rigid_groups[].body            a body id you emit
  joints[].parent_group/child_group  rigid group ids you emit
  interfaces[].bodies            body ids you emit
  configurations[].bodies_present body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].reach_targets functional region ids you emit
  functional_regions[].required_by_actors actor ids from the input
  joints[].frame_ids             frame names you coin here
  bodies[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  interfaces[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].rigid_group  a rigid group id you emit
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].differs_from configuration ids you emit
  unresolved[].kept_open_by      Ambiguity or Freedom ids from the input, and
                                 nothing else - not a requirement, not a body
  unresolved[].alternatives      when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS these are
                                 entity ids; otherwise they are not ids at all

identity list and nothing more - it says which ids are taken, not
what those entities say, and it is not something to reason from.

commonly the one already taken.

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. rendered prompt (41740 chars)

You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW
   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.
   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are
   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left
   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the
   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable
   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-
   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a
   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups
   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at
   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.
6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it
   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could
   cross.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity,
                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body
                       is the reason for; [] if none)
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]
                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed
                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. ["FRM-JNT-0001"].
                       "+Z" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that
                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the
                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later
                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.
                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint
                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,
                       and [] is the right answer there.
                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT
                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another
                       object:
                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,
                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,
                         activation_window
                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real
                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this
                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so
                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence
                       that the mechanism deflects itself.
                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.
                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have
                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not
                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as
                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result
                       nothing here computed.
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,
                       addresses_obligations[]
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[],
                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}
                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the
                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the
                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required
                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and
                       is checked against it, so a name is never what
                       distinguishes two states
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[],
                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for
                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),
                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region
                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the
                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from
                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the
                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor
                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on
                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)
  unresolved[]         id "S3U-0001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT
  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ
  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE
  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

IDS YOU EMIT ARE NEW
Every id in your response is one you are creating now. The typed input already
contains ids of its own, and reusing one of them does not extend that entity, it
collides with it. Use exactly the prefixes shown above and never an id that
already appears in the input.

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
  rigid_groups[].body            a body id you emit
  joints[].parent_group/child_group  rigid group ids you emit
  interfaces[].bodies            body ids you emit
  configurations[].bodies_present body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit
  functional_regions[].reach_targets functional region ids you emit
  functional_regions[].required_by_actors actor ids from the input
  joints[].frame_ids             frame names you coin here
  bodies[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  interfaces[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].rigid_group  a rigid group id you emit
  configurations[].distinguishing_basis[].differs_from configuration ids you emit
  unresolved[].kept_open_by      Ambiguity or Freedom ids from the input, and
                                 nothing else - not a requirement, not a body
  unresolved[].alternatives      when alternatives_kind is ENTITY_REFS these are
                                 entity ids; otherwise they are not ids at all

    "prompt_text": "You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,\nhow they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,\nand in what order the thing goes together.\n\nYou receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.\n\nWHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT\nGeometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies\ntouch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a\npart is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and\nno axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not\nexist yet. Saying \"the axis points +Z\" is this stage's work. Saying \"the axis is\n40 mm from the base\" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.\n\nRULES\n1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a\n   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give\n   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group\n   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four\n   groups and four joints, not one region.\n2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of\n   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.\n3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify HOW\n   THEY MEET: CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION.\n   This is not a joint type: FIXED, REVOLUTE and the rest say how two groups are\n   CONSTRAINED, and belong on joints. A body pair that meets and is left\n   unclassified is a hole in the design. On each body and interface, list the\n   obligation ids it is the reason for - the design decision has to be traceable\n   to the obligation that forced it, or nothing downstream can tell a load-\n   bearing choice from an arbitrary one.\n4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism\n   can be in that matter to its function.\n5. Every degree of freedom of every rigid group in every configuration becomes a\n   line the pipeline enumerates from what you declare here, so make the groups\n   and configurations complete and final. A group you leave out has no lines at\n   all, and a line that does not exist cannot be reported as unexplained.\n6. A later step traces the load paths and the assembly order. Give it what it\n   needs: every body a load could pass through, and every interface it could\n   cross.\n9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be\nempty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.\n\n  bodies[]             id \"BOD-0001\", role, instance_identity,\n                       addresses_obligations[] (obligation ids this body\n                       is the reason for; [] if none)\n  rigid_groups[]       id \"RGP-0001\", body, members[], is_default (boolean)\n  joints[]             id \"JNT-0001\", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,\n                       dof[], axis_direction, frame_ids[]\n                       frame_ids NAMES THE FRAME the axis_direction is expressed\n                       in - a symbolic name you coin here, e.g. [\"FRM-JNT-0001\"].\n                       \"+Z\" relative to nothing is unanswerable, so a joint that\n                       states a real direction must name one. You are naming the\n                       frame, not locating it: WHERE it sits is decided later\n                       from feature sizes that do not exist yet.\n                       A joint whose axis_direction is NONE - a FIXED joint\n                       constrains everything and points nowhere - needs no frame,\n                       and [] is the right answer there.\n                       For a COMPLIANT joint, and only then, add these EIGHT\n                       fields DIRECTLY ON THE JOINT - not nested inside another\n                       object:\n                         mode, direction, required_travel, allowable_travel,\n                         actuation, compliant_element, root_interface,\n                         activation_window\n                       actuation is always PRESCRIBED_KINEMATIC - in the real\n                       mechanism a contact drives the deflection, but in this\n                       model the coordinate is imposed, and the field says so\n                       precisely so the structure cannot be read as evidence\n                       that the mechanism deflects itself.\n                       required_travel is KINEMATIC and is yours to state.\n                       allowable_travel is a MATERIAL fact and you do not have\n                       the material: report its status as UNSUPPORTED. Do not\n                       write a number, and do not write a verdict such as\n                       WITHIN_ELASTIC_LIMIT - that would assert a strain result\n                       nothing here computed.\n  interfaces[]         id \"IFC-0001\", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal,\n                       addresses_obligations[]\n  configurations[]     id \"CFG-0001\", name, kind, bodies_present[],\n                       distinguishing_basis[] {rigid_group, dof, differs_from[]}\n                       - what makes this configuration a DIFFERENT one: the\n                       (rigid group, DOF) pairs whose value differs from the\n                       named sibling configurations. [] when nothing is required\n                       to differ. A later step realizes this in coordinates and\n                       is checked against it, so a name is never what\n                       distinguishes two states\n  functional_regions[] id \"FRG-0001\", role, owning_bodies[],\n                       required_by_actors[] (actor ids from the input; [] for\n                       SUPPORT and KEEP_OUT regions no actor uses),\n                       reach_targets[] (OTHER functional region ids THIS region\n                       gives reach through to - an APERTURE's targets are the\n                       ACCESS regions reached through it. Region ids only, from\n                       the ones you emit here; [] when this region is itself the\n                       destination. It is NOT a description of what an actor\n                       wants: that demand is already typed upstream on\n                       Actor.must_reach and is not restated here)\n  unresolved[]         id \"S3U-0001\", decision, why_open, alternatives[],\n                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]\n\nPERMITTED VALUES\n  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT\n  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ\n  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE\n  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION\n  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE\n  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT\n\nIDS YOU EMIT ARE NEW\nEvery id in your response is one you are creating now. functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit\n  functional_regions[].reach_targets functional region ids you emit\n  functional_regions[].required_by_actors actor ids from the input\n  joints[].frame_ids             frame names you coin here\n  bodies[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input\n  interfaces[].addresses_obligations obligation ids from the input\n
